profile_text.body:
Arm is a for-profit public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. On its own site the company describes itself as providing the compute platforms behind advanced AI, connecting cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software, flexible compute, and an ecosystem it says is built to scale intelligence everywhere. It says it delivers performance, efficiency, and flexibility for cloud and personal devices, AI-defined vehicles, and robotics, and that it enables scalable orchestration across cloud and edge environments as data centers operate as coordinated systems.

Among the AI efforts named on the site is the Arm AI Portal, which the company describes as giving developers and agents one place to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, access deployment workflows, or optimize their own models for Arm. The site also refers to an AGI CPU launched by Arm, with Arm's Eddie Ramirez explaining the reasoning behind it and describing agentic AI as reshaping data centers and efficiency as becoming the defining metric for the AI era. Arm Create events in Shanghai and Shenzhen are cited as showcasing ecosystem work on intelligent applications, AGIBOT is cited as showing a common Arm compute platform connecting AI, perception, motion, and control in robots, and NVIDIA DGX Spark is described as built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology for running large models locally.

The record holds no litigation involving Arm. The MCP servers listed under the Arm name are third-party tools, including ones for data observability, calendar access, contractor search, career frameworks, drug information, ad bidding, pharma vendor services, and a fishing game, and the site text does not connect any of them to Arm.
